claims.source: In addition, we found that psr-1; ttr-52 double mutants show no significant enhancement of puncta defects compared to either single mutant, suggesting that PSR-1 and TTR-52 function within the same pathway for PS recognition by AMsh glia (Figure 4D).
claims.evidence: This conclusion is based on the genetic epistasis analysis shown in Figure 4D.

claims.claim: A mutation in ina-1 has no effect on NRE engulfment.
claims.source: Integrins function with MeRTK to promote photoreceptor cell outer segment engulfment by retinal RPE glia (Mao and Finnemann, 2012), and the C. elegans genome encodes two α-integrin subunits, INA-1 and PAT-2, both of which are implicated in apoptotic cell phagocytosis in C. elegans (Hsieh et al., 2012; Neukomm et al., 2014; Sáenz-Narciso et al., 2016). We found that while a mutation in ina-1 has no effect on NRE engulfment (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A), loss of PAT-2 by RNA interference (RNAi) significantly blocks AFD–NRE phagocytosis (Figure 4G).
claims.evidence: Figure 4—figure supplement 1A shows that ina-1 mutants have normal puncta levels.

claims.claim: Loss of PAT-2 by RNA interference significantly blocks AFD–NRE phagocytosis.
claims.source: We found that while a mutation in ina-1 has no effect on NRE engulfment (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A), loss of PAT-2 by RNA interference (RNAi) significantly blocks AFD–NRE phagocytosis (Figure 4G).
claims.evidence: Figure 4G shows that pat-2 RNAi reduces puncta in wild-type animals.

claims.claim: pat-2 RNAi strongly enhances glia engulfment defects of psr-1 mutants.
claims.source: Further, pat-2 RNAi strongly enhances glia engulfment defects of psr-1 mutants (Figure 4G).
claims.evidence: Figure 4G shows that pat-2 RNAi in psr-1 mutants results in a more severe reduction in puncta than either perturbation alone.

claims.claim: PAT-2/α-integrin and PSR-1 appear to act together for glial engulfment of AFD–NRE.
claims.source: Thus, PAT-2/α-integrin and PSR-1 appear to act together for glial engulfment of AFD–NRE.
claims.evidence: This conclusion is based on the genetic interaction data shown in Figure 4G.

claims.claim: ced-1(e1754) strong loss-of-function mutant animals exhibit enhanced puncta numbers compared to wild-type animals.
claims.source: Curiously, not only do mutations in ced-1 not block the appearance of puncta in glia, we found that ced-1(e1754) strong loss-of-function mutant animals actually exhibit enhanced puncta numbers compared to wild-type animals (Figure 4C).
claims.evidence: Figure 4C shows that ced-1 mutants have more puncta than wild type.

claims.claim: Animals bearing mutations in ced-2, ced-5, or ced-12 exhibit reduced AFD–NRE puncta in AMsh glia.
claims.source: The ternary complex of CED-2/CrkII, CED-5/DOCK1, and CED-12/ELMO1 acts downstream of PSR-1 for apoptotic cell engulfment (Reddien and Horvitz, 2004; Wang et al., 2003). We found that animals bearing mutations in ced-2, ced-5, or ced-12 exhibit reduced AFD–NRE puncta in AMsh glia (Figure 5A).
claims.evidence: Figure 5A shows that ced-2, ced-5, and ced-12 mutants all have reduced puncta compared to wild type.

claims.claim: Expression of the CED-12B isoform in AMsh glia is sufficient to rescue ced-12 mutant defects.
claims.source: Furthermore, expression of the CED-12B isoform in AMsh glia is sufficient to rescue ced-12 mutant defects (Figure 5A).
claims.evidence: Figure 5A shows that glial-specific expression of CED-12 rescues the ced-12 mutant phenotype.

claims.claim: The CED-2/CED-5/CED-12 complex likely regulates engulfment of AFD–NREs.
claims.source: We conclude, therefore, that the CED-2/CED-5/CED-12 complex also likely regulates engulfment of AFD–NREs.
claims.evidence: This conclusion is based on the mutant and rescue data shown in Figure 5A.

claims.claim: Two loss-of-function mutations in ced-10 block nearly all engulfment of AFD–NRE fragments by AMsh glia.
claims.source: We found that two loss-of-function mutations in ced-10, or overexpression of dominant-negative CED-10T17N, block nearly all engulfment of AFD–NRE fragments by AMsh glia (Figure 5B–D).
claims.evidence: Figure 5B-D shows that ced-10 mutants have very few puncta in glia.

claims.claim: Overexpression of dominant-negative CED-10T17N blocks nearly all engulfment of AFD–NRE fragments by AMsh glia.
claims.source: We found that two loss-of-function mutations in ced-10, or overexpression of dominant-negative CED-10T17N, block nearly all engulfment of AFD–NRE fragments by AMsh glia (Figure 5B–D).
claims.evidence: Figure 5D shows that expression of dominant-negative CED-10 blocks puncta formation.

claims.claim: psr-1; ced-10 and ced-12; ced-10 double mutants show strong defects in puncta numbers reminiscent of ced-10 single mutants.
claims.source: To determine how CED-10 functions with respect to CED-2/CED-5/CED-12 and PSR-1, we generated psr-1; ced-10 and ced-12; ced-10 double mutants. Both strains show strong defects in puncta numbers reminiscent of ced-10 single mutants (Figure 5E).
claims.evidence: Figure 5E shows epistasis analysis indicating that ced-10 is epistatic to psr-1 and ced-12.

claims.claim: Transgenic expression of CED-10 is sufficient to overcome the partial loss of NRE engulfment in psr-1 mutants.
claims.source: Furthermore, transgenic expression of CED-10 is sufficient to overcome the partial loss of NRE engulfment in psr-1 mutants (Figure 5E).
claims.evidence: Figure 5E shows that CED-10 overexpression in psr-1 mutants increases puncta numbers.

claims.claim: CED-10/Rac1 GTPase likely functions in glia downstream of CED-2/CED-5/CED-12 and PSR-1 to promote AMsh glial engulfment of NREs.
claims.source: Our data are consistent with the interpretation that, like in cell corpse engulfment, CED-10/Rac1 GTPase likely functions in glia downstream of CED-2/CED-5/CED-12 and PSR-1, to promote AMsh glial engulfment of NREs.
claims.evidence: This conclusion is based on epistasis analysis shown in Figure 5E and comparison to known apoptotic phagocytosis pathways.

claims.claim: Mutations in unc-73/TRIO do not affect NRE uptake.
claims.source: This activation is specific as mutations in another CED-10 activator, UNC-73/TRIO, do not affect NRE uptake (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A; Lundquist et al., 2001; Sáenz-Narciso et al., 2016).
claims.evidence: Figure 4—figure supplement 1A shows that unc-73 mutants have normal puncta levels.

claims.claim: Expression of constitutive active CED-10G12V results in reduced engulfed puncta.
claims.source: Unexpectedly, expression of constitutive active CED-10G12V also results in reduced engulfed puncta (Figure 5D).
claims.evidence: Figure 5D shows that expression of constitutively active CED-10 reduces puncta numbers.

claims.claim: The AFD–NRE is significantly shorter in CED-10G12V mutants.
claims.source: Supporting the latter model, the AFD–NRE is significantly shorter in CED-10G12V mutants (see below).
claims.evidence: This refers to data shown later in Figure 7—figure supplement 1, which shows shortened NRE in CED-10G12V animals.

claims.claim: Overexpression of wild-type CED-10, but not of wild-type PSR-1 or CED-12, increases NRE engulfment.
claims.source: Furthermore, overexpression of wild-type CED-10, but not of wild-type PSR-1 or CED-12, increases NRE engulfment Figure 4D, Figure 5A,D).
claims.evidence: Figures 4D and 5A,D show that only CED-10 overexpression, not PSR-1 or CED-12, increases puncta numbers.

claims.claim: Glial CED-10 is both necessary and sufficient to regulate the rate at which AMsh glial engulf AFD–NRE fragments.
claims.source: Glial CED-10 is, therefore, both necessary and sufficient to regulate the rate at which AMsh glial engulf AFD–NRE fragments.
claims.evidence: This conclusion is based on loss-of-function, rescue, and overexpression experiments shown in Figure 5.

claims.claim: Animals bearing a loss-of-function mutation in wsp-1 show a block in NRE engulfment.
claims.source: During apoptotic cell engulfment, CED-10 executes phagocytic arm extension by mediating actin remodeling (Wang and Yang, 2016). We, therefore, examined animals bearing a loss-of-function mutation in wsp-1, which encodes an actin polymerization factor, and found a block in NRE engulfment (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
claims.evidence: Figure 5—figure supplement 1A shows that wsp-1 mutants have reduced puncta.

claims.claim: Increasing levels of WSP-1 specifically in AMsh glia leads to increased NRE engulfment.
claims.source: As with overexpression of CED-10, increasing levels of WSP-1 specifically in AMsh glia also lead to increased NRE engulfment (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
claims.evidence: Figure 5—figure supplement 1A shows that WSP-1 overexpression in glia increases puncta numbers.

claims.claim: CED-10-dependent actin remodeling is the rate-limiting step for the engulfment of AFD–NREs by glia.
claims.source: These results suggest that CED-10-dependent actin remodeling is the rate-limiting step for the engulfment of AFD–NREs by glia.
claims.evidence: This conclusion is based on the observation that both CED-10 and WSP-1 overexpression increase engulfment rates.

claims.claim: Cyclic-nucleotide-gated (CNG) ion channels localize to the AFD cilium base and are required for AFD neuron firing in response to temperature stimuli.
claims.source: Previous studies showed that cyclic-nucleotide-gated (CNG) ion channels localize to the AFD cilium base and are required for AFD neuron firing in response to temperature stimuli (Cho et al., 2004; Ramot et al., 2008; Satterlee et al., 2004).
claims.evidence: This is a summary of findings from previous studies, supported by citations.

claims.claim: CNG channels are mis-localized in cilia-defective mutants.
claims.source: These channels are mis-localized in cilia-defective mutants (Nguyen et al., 2014).
claims.evidence: This is based on a citation to previous work.

claims.claim: Cilia-defective mutants exhibit deficits in thermotaxis behavior.
claims.source: Independently, it has been shown that cilia-defective mutants exhibit deficits in thermotaxis behavior (Tan et al., 2007).
claims.evidence: This is based on a citation to previous work.

claims.claim: tax-2 mutant glia accumulate extra puncta.
claims.source: We examined animals defective in TAX-2, the sole CNG β-subunit in the C. elegans genome, or in TAX-4 and CNG-3, α-subunits that function together in AFD (Cho et al., 2004; Hellman and Shen, 2011; Satterlee et al., 2004) for engulfment defects. Glia in mutant animals accumulate extra puncta (tax-2: 28.1 ± 2 puncta, n = 37; tax-4; cng-3 double mutants: 23.8 ± 2.3 puncta, n = 17) (Figure 6A–C)
claims.evidence: Figure 6A-C shows that tax-2 and tax-4; cng-3 mutants have increased puncta compared to wild type.

claims.claim: tax-4; cng-3 double mutant glia accumulate extra puncta.
claims.source: We examined animals defective in TAX-2, the sole CNG β-subunit in the C. elegans genome, or in TAX-4 and CNG-3, α-subunits that function together in AFD (Cho et al., 2004; Hellman and Shen, 2011; Satterlee et al., 2004) for engulfment defects. Glia in mutant animals accumulate extra puncta (tax-2: 28.1 ± 2 puncta, n = 37; tax-4; cng-3 double mutants: 23.8 ± 2.3 puncta, n = 17) (Figure 6A–C)
claims.evidence: Figure 6A-C shows that tax-2 and tax-4; cng-3 mutants have increased puncta compared to wild type.

claims.claim: In tax-2 mutants, a larger fraction of the animal population has >10 puncta compared to wild type.
claims.source: and in tax-2 mutants, a larger fraction of the animal population has >10 puncta (tax-2, 99%, n = 92 animals; wild type, 65%, n = 171 animals) (Figure 6C).
claims.evidence: Figure 6C shows population distribution data comparing tax-2 mutants to wild type.

claims.claim: pde-1; pde-5 double mutant animals have reduced glia puncta numbers compared to wild type.
claims.source: Conversely, we assessed the consequence of increasing the levels of cGMP, which promotes CNG channel opening, by mutating the cGMP degrading enzymes PDE-1 and PDE-5 expressed in AFD neurons (Ramot et al., 2008; Singhvi et al., 2016). We found that pde-1; pde-5 double mutant animals have reduced glia puncta numbers compared to wild type (7.1 ± 1.4, n = 11 vs. 14 ± 1, n = 78) (Figure 6B, C).
claims.evidence: Figure 6B and 6C show that pde-1; pde-5 mutants have fewer puncta than wild type.

claims.claim: Acute and cell-specific chemogenetic silencing of AFD leads to puncta enrichment in AMsh glia within 24 hr.
claims.source: Finally, acute and cell-specific chemogenetic silencing of AFD using a histamine-gated chloride channel (Pokala et al., 2014) expressed under an AFD-specific promoter leads to puncta enrichment in AMsh glia within 24 hr (Figure 6E, F).
claims.evidence: Figure 6E and 6F show that histamine treatment of animals expressing HisCl1 in AFD increases puncta in glia.

claims.claim: AFD activity levels reciprocally affect AFD–NRE engulfment levels.
claims.source: Thus, AFD activity levels reciprocally affect AFD–NRE engulfment levels and can do so acutely.
claims.evidence: This conclusion is based on the combined data from activity mutants and chemogenetic silencing experiments shown in Figure 6.

claims.claim: The increase in puncta number seen in tax-2 mutant glia is entirely suppressed by loss of CED-10.
claims.source: Accumulation of glial puncta in AFD activity mutants could result from increased engulfment rates or, alternatively, from decreased puncta degradation. We favor the former model as we found that the increase in puncta number seen in tax-2 mutant glia is entirely suppressed by loss of CED-10 (Figure 6B, C).
claims.evidence: Figure 6B and 6C show that tax-2; ced-10 double mutants have puncta levels similar to ced-10 single mutants.

claims.claim: Significant suppression is observed in tax-2; psr-1(tm469) double mutants compared to tax-2 alone.
claims.source: Likewise, we also observed significant suppression in tax-2; psr-1(tm469) double mutants compared to tax-2 alone; and this suppression is enhanced further by pat-2 (RNAi) (Figure 6C, D).
claims.evidence: Figure 6C and 6D show epistasis analysis of tax-2 with psr-1 and pat-2.

claims.claim: Loss of ced-10 suppresses excess engulfment following acute chemogenetic silencing of AFD.
claims.source: Loss of ced-10 also suppresses excess engulfment following acute chemogenetic silencing of AFD (Figure 6F).
claims.evidence: Figure 6F shows that ced-10 mutants do not show increased puncta upon histamine treatment.

claims.claim: Neuron activity controls NRE engulfment through the CED-10 pathway.
claims.source: Our findings are therefore consistent with neuron activity controlling NRE engulfment through the CED-10 pathway.
claims.evidence: This conclusion is based on the epistasis experiments shown in Figure 6.

claims.claim: ced-10 loss of function results in elongated AFD–NRE microvilli.
claims.source: We found that ced-10 loss of function, or AMsh glia-specific overexpression of dominant negative CED-10T17N, results in elongated AFD–NRE microvilli (Figure 7A, B, Figure 7—figure supplement 1B).
claims.evidence: Figure 7A, B, and Figure 7—figure supplement 1B show that ced-10 mutants have longer NRE microvilli.

claims.claim: AMsh glia-specific overexpression of dominant negative CED-10T17N results in elongated AFD–NRE microvilli.
claims.source: We found that ced-10 loss of function, or AMsh glia-specific overexpression of dominant negative CED-10T17N, results in elongated AFD–NRE microvilli (Figure 7A, B, Figure 7—figure supplement 1B).
claims.evidence: Figure 7A, B, and Figure 7—figure supplement 1B show that dominant-negative CED-10 expression in glia causes longer NRE microvilli.

claims.claim: Overexpressing wild-type CED-10 produces shorter AFD–NRE microvilli.
claims.source: By contrast, overexpressing wild-type CED-10, which has excess puncta, produces shorter AFD–NRE microvilli, and this defect worsens with age (Figure 7A, B).
claims.evidence: Figure 7A and B show that CED-10 overexpression results in shorter NRE microvilli.

claims.claim: The defect in AFD-NRE microvilli length from CED-10 overexpression worsens with age.
claims.source: By contrast, overexpressing wild-type CED-10, which has excess puncta, produces shorter AFD–NRE microvilli, and this defect worsens with age (Figure 7A, B).
claims.evidence: Figure 7B shows that the proportion of animals with defective NRE increases from day 1 to day 3 in CED-10 overexpression strains.

claims.claim: Overexpressing GTP-locked CED10G12V leads to shorter AFD–NRE microvilli.
claims.source: Furthermore, overexpressing GTP-locked CED10G12V also leads to shorter AFD–NRE microvilli even though it paradoxically has reduced number of puncta in glia (Figure 7—figure supplement 1A, B)
claims.evidence: Figure 7—figure supplement 1A and B show that constitutively active CED-10 expression results in shorter NRE microvilli.

claims.claim: AMsh glial engulfment of NRE fragments is important for regulating the AFD–NRE microvilli length.
claims.source: Thus, AMsh glial engulfment of NRE fragments is important for regulating the AFD–NRE microvilli length.
claims.evidence: This conclusion is based on the correlation between engulfment levels and NRE length shown in Figure 7.

claims.claim: C. elegans seek their temperature of cultivation (Tc) when placed on a temperature gradient.
claims.source: When placed on a temperature gradient, C. elegans seek their temperature of cultivation, Tc (Hedgecock and Russell, 1975; Figure 7C–F, wild-type data in black line).
claims.evidence: This is a well-established behavior supported by citations and shown in Figure 7C-F.

claims.claim: This animal behavior depends on thermosensory transduction at the AFD–NRE.
claims.source: This animal behavior depends on thermosensory transduction at the AFD–NRE (Goodman and Sengupta, 2018; Mori and Ohshima, 1995).
claims.evidence: This is based on citations to previous work on thermotaxis behavior.

claims.claim: Animals with defects in AFD–NRE shape exhibit defects in thermosensory behavior.
claims.source: Previous studies have shown that animals with defects in AFD–NRE shape also exhibit defects in this thermosensory behavior.
claims.evidence: This is a summary of findings from previous studies, though specific citations are not provided in this sentence.

claims.claim: ced-10 mutants exhibit altered thermosensory behavior.
claims.source: Consistent with this, we found that ced-10 mutants exhibit altered thermosensory behavior.
claims.evidence: This is supported by the thermotaxis assay data shown in Figure 7C-D.

claims.claim: While wild-type animals reared at 25°C migrate to their Tc = 25°C on a linear temperature gradient, ced-10 mutants prefer cooler temperatures.
claims.source: While wild-type animals reared at 25°C migrate to their Tc = 25°C on a linear temperature gradient, ced-10 mutants prefer cooler temperatures (Figure 7C, D).
claims.evidence: Figure 7C and D show thermotaxis behavior data comparing wild type and ced-10 mutants.

claims.claim: Animals carrying integrated transgenes overexpressing CED-10 only in AMsh glia exhibit athermotactic defects regardless of the cultivation temperatures.
claims.source: Furthermore, animals carrying integrated transgenes overexpressing CED-10 only in AMsh glia also exhibit athermotactic defects regardless of the cultivation temperatures (Figure 7E, F).
claims.evidence: Figure 7E and F show thermotaxis behavior data for CED-10 overexpression strains at different cultivation temperatures.

claims.claim: AFD–NRE engulfment by AMsh glia is required for appropriate animal thermotaxis behaviors.
claims.source: We conclude, therefore, that AFD–NRE engulfment by AMsh glia is required for appropriate animal thermotaxis behaviors.
claims.evidence: This conclusion is based on the correlation between engulfment defects and behavioral defects shown in Figure 7.

claims.claim: The athermotactic behavior of CED-10 overexpression strains mimics similar defects of tax-2 or tax-2; tax-4 double mutant animals.
claims.source: The behavior defects we observed are consistent with the thesis that reduced neuron activity drives glial engulfment. The athermotactic behavior of CED-10 overexpression strains mimics similar defects of tax-2 or tax-2; tax-4 double mutant animals, and both manipulations lead to increased puncta and reduced neuron activity (Figure 7—figure supplement 1C, D; Cho et al., 2004; Satterlee et al., 2004).
claims.evidence: Figure 7—figure supplement 1C and D show thermotaxis behavior data for tax-2 and tax-4 mutants, and citations support the connection to neuron activity.

claims.claim: The cryophilic behavior of ced-10 mutants is similar to that observed in other mutants with increased AFD cGMP levels.
claims.source: Likewise, the cryophilic behavior of ced-10 mutants, which have reduced glia puncta, is similar to that observed in other mutants with increased AFD cGMP levels (Singhvi et al., 2016).
claims.evidence: This comparison is based on the thermotaxis data in Figure 7 and a citation to previous work on cGMP mutants.

claims.claim: Activity-dependent glial engulfment of NRE is one mechanism by which AMsh glia and AFD coordinate regulation of NRE shape and animal thermosensory behavior.
claims.source: We favor the model that activity-dependent glial engulfment of NRE is one mechanism by which AMsh glia and AFD coordinate regulation of NRE shape and animal thermosensory behavior.
claims.evidence: This is a model proposed based on the combined data from Figures 6 and 7.

claims.claim: C. elegans glia share molecular, morphological, and functional features with vertebrate sense-organ glia and astrocytes.
claims.source: Glia of the nematode C. elegans share molecular, morphological, and functional features with vertebrate sense-organ glia and astrocytes (Bacaj et al., 2008a; Katz et al., 2018; Katz et al., 2019; Lee et al., 2021; Singhvi and Shaham, 2019; Wallace et al., 2016).
claims.evidence: This is a summary statement supported by multiple citations to previous work.

claims.claim: Glial CED-10 levels dictate engulfment rates.
claims.source: Exploiting unique features of our experimental model, we demonstrate that glial CED-10 levels dictate engulfment rates, revealing that glia drive neuronal remodeling and do not just passively clear shed neuronal debris.
claims.evidence: This is supported by the data in Figure 5 showing that CED-10 overexpression increases engulfment and loss-of-function decreases it.

claims.claim: Glia drive neuronal remodeling and do not just passively clear shed neuronal debris.
claims.source: Exploiting unique features of our experimental model, we demonstrate that glial CED-10 levels dictate engulfment rates, revealing that glia drive neuronal remodeling and do not just passively clear shed neuronal debris.
claims.evidence: This conclusion is based on the finding that glial CED-10 levels control engulfment rates and NRE shape.

claims.claim: Engulfment is required for post-developmental maintenance of sensory NRE shape and behavior.
claims.source: Indeed, we demonstrate that engulfment is required for post-developmental maintenance of sensory NRE shape and behavior.
claims.evidence: This is supported by the data in Figure 7 showing that engulfment defects lead to altered NRE shape and behavior in adults.

claims.claim: Glial engulfment extends a role for glial engulfment in the active sensory perception of temperature.
claims.source: This also extends a role for glial engulfment in the active sensory perception of temperature.
claims.evidence: This is based on the finding that engulfment affects thermosensory behavior shown in Figure 7.

claims.claim: Pruning of individual neurons by a single glia modifies animal behavior.
claims.source: Importantly, our studies allow us to directly demonstrate at single-cell resolution that pruning of individual neurons by a single glia modifies animal behavior.
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by the correlation between glial engulfment of AFD and thermotaxis behavior shown in Figure 7.

claims.claim: Phagocytosis is impacted by neuronal activity states.
claims.source: This, in conjunction with our finding that phagocytosis is impacted by neuronal activity states, demonstrates important physiological relevance.
claims.evidence: This is supported by the data in Figure 6 showing that neuron activity mutants have altered engulfment.

claims.claim: Glia-dependent phagocytosis can be dynamically tuned throughout animal life to modulate NRE morphology, impacting animal behavior.
claims.source: Our studies reveal a fundamental distinction between glia-dependent phagocytosis and other modes of engulfment. Apoptotic cell phagocytosis, glial clearance of injury-induced neuronal debris, and related engulfment events are all-or-none phenomena: engulfment either occurs or does not. By contrast, we show here that in AMsh glia engulfment rate is dynamically tuned throughout animal life to modulate NRE morphology, impacting animal behavior.
claims.evidence: This is based on the developmental time course data in Figure 2 and the activity-dependent regulation shown in Figure 6.

claims.claim: Controlled phagocytosis may similarly regulate glial engulfment in other settings.
claims.source: The molecular parallels between the engulfment machinery in the peripheral sense-organ AMsh glia and other CNS glial engulfment lead us to posit that controlled phagocytosis may similarly regulate glial engulfment in other settings.
claims.evidence: This is a speculation based on the molecular conservation of the engulfment pathway.

claims.claim: Apoptotic phagocytosis in C. elegans relies predominantly on CED-1, with the PS-receptor PSR-1 playing a minor role.
claims.source: Apoptotic phagocytosis in C. elegans relies predominantly on CED-1, with the PS-receptor PSR-1 playing a minor role (Wang et al., 2003; Wang and Yang, 2016).
claims.evidence: This is a summary of findings from previous studies, supported by citations.

claims.claim: CED-1 is dispensable for pruning by AMsh glia.
claims.source: Surprisingly, while CED-1 is dispensable for pruning by AMsh glia, we identified PSR-1/PS-receptor as a novel regulator of glial pruning.
claims.evidence: This is supported by the data in Figure 4C showing that ced-1 mutants still have puncta in glia.

claims.claim: PSR-1/PS-receptor is a novel regulator of glial pruning.
claims.source: Surprisingly, while CED-1 is dispensable for pruning by AMsh glia, we identified PSR-1/PS-receptor as a novel regulator of glial pruning.
claims.evidence: This is supported by the data in Figure 4D-E showing that psr-1 mutants have reduced puncta.

claims.claim: Engulfment of small cell process debris of the C. elegans tail-spike cell is independent of CED-1.
claims.source: One possibility is that this difference in receptors reflects the size of particles engulfed. Supporting this notion, engulfment of small cell process debris of the C. elegans tail-spike cell is also independent of CED-1 (Ghose et al., 2018).
claims.evidence: This is based on a citation to previous work on tail-spike cell debris engulfment.

claims.claim: Other PS-receptors that regulate glial engulfment across species include CED-1/MEGF10/Draper, MerTK, and GPR56.
claims.source: Other PS-receptors that have been shown to regulate glial engulfment across species include CED-1/MEGF10/Draper, MerTK, and GPR56, and it is likely that yet others await identification (Chung et al., 2013; Freeman, 2015; Hilu-Dadia and Kurant, 2020; Kevany and Palczewski, 2010; Li et al., 2020; Nomura-Komoike et al., 2020; Raiders et al., 2021; Tasdemir-Yilmaz and Freeman, 2014; Vecino et al., 2016).
claims.evidence: This is a summary of findings from multiple previous studies, supported by citations.

claims.claim: Murine P4-ATPases ATP8A1 and ATP8A2 are expressed in the nervous system.
claims.source: We note that murine P4-ATPases ATP8A1 and ATP8A2 are expressed in the nervous system, and knockout mice exhibit deficient hippocampal learning, sensory deficits, cerebellar ataxia, mental retardation, and spinal cord degeneration, and shortened photoreceptor NRE length (Coleman et al., 2014).
claims.evidence: This is based on a citation to previous work on murine ATP8A knockout mice.

claims.claim: Murine ATP8A knockout mice exhibit deficient hippocampal learning, sensory deficits, cerebellar ataxia, mental retardation, spinal cord degeneration, and shortened photoreceptor NRE length.
claims.source: We note that murine P4-ATPases ATP8A1 and ATP8A2 are expressed in the nervous system, and knockout mice exhibit deficient hippocampal learning, sensory deficits, cerebellar ataxia, mental retardation, and spinal cord degeneration, and shortened photoreceptor NRE length (Coleman et al., 2014).
claims.evidence: This is based on a citation to previous work on murine ATP8A knockout mice.

claims.claim: TTR-52 is implicated in apoptotic phagocytosis and nerve regeneration.
claims.source: We also identify the PS bridging molecule TTR-52 as a regulator of pruning. It is also implicated in apoptotic phagocytosis and nerve regeneration (Neumann et al., 2015; Wang et al., 2010).
claims.evidence: This is based on citations to previous work on TTR-52 function.

claims.claim: Retinal RPE glia and cortical astrocytes require PS-bridging opsonins (Gas6 and MFGE8) to engulf neuron fragments.
claims.source: Retinal RPE glia and cortical astrocytes also require PS-bridging opsonins (Gas6 and MFGE8) to engulf neuron fragments (Bellesi et al., 2017; Kevany and Palczewski, 2010).
claims.evidence: This is based on citations to previous work on opsonins in mammalian glia.

claims.claim: Aberrantly excessive/reduced pruning correlate with disease in mammals.
claims.source: Aberrantly excessive/reduced pruning correlate with disease in mammals, hinting that similar subcellular precision in marking fragments/endings for engulfment might be involved (Chung et al., 2015; Wilton et al., 2019).
claims.evidence: This is based on citations to previous work on pruning defects in disease.

claims.claim: Peripheral glia of the inner ear activate phagocytosis only in injury settings.
claims.source: Peripheral glia of the inner ear are known to activate phagocytosis only in injury settings (Bird et al., 2010).
claims.evidence: This is based on a citation to previous work on inner ear glia.

claims.claim: Glial pruning is conserved in both CNS and PNS and is executed for normal neural functions by analogous molecular mechanisms.
claims.source: Our studies demonstrate that pruning of sensory neuron endings by glia is required for accurate sensory perception. Thus, glial pruning is conserved in both CNS and PNS and is executed for normal neural functions by analogous molecular mechanisms.
claims.evidence: This conclusion is based on the findings that AMsh glia (PNS) use similar molecular machinery to CNS glia for pruning.

claims.claim: AMsh glia and AFD neuron cooperate through multiple mechanisms to regulate AFD–NRE shape and animal thermosensory behaviors.
claims.source: While these studies identify glial pruning as a mechanism to control NRE shape in response to activity states, we note that it is likely that AMsh glia and AFD neuron cooperate through multiple mechanisms to regulate AFD–NRE shape and animal thermosensory behaviors, including some that we previously identified (Singhvi et al., 2016; Wallace et al., 2016).
claims.evidence: This is based on the current findings combined with citations to previous work from the same group.

claims.claim: Appropriate thermosensory behaviors are critical for animal survival.
claims.source: Such regulatory complexity might reflect the fact that appropriate thermosensory behaviors are critical for animal survival.
claims.evidence: This is a speculation based on general biological knowledge about the importance of sensory behaviors.

claims.claim: Glial CED-10 levels can modulate engulfment rates, NRE shape, and animal behavior.
claims.source: Three lines of evidence in this study lead us to conclude that AMsh glia actively drive engulfment rather than passively clearing debris. (1) Our finding that glial CED-10 levels can modulate engulfment rates, NRE shape, and animal behavior suggests that this process can be triggered by glia.
claims.evidence: This is supported by the data in Figures 5 and 7 showing that CED-10 levels affect engulfment, NRE shape, and behavior.

claims.claim: Short NRE shape can derive from independent mechanisms.
claims.source: (2) While both CED-10 overexpression and ttx-1 mutants have short NRE (Satterlee et al., 2001; Figure 4—figure supplement 1B), unlike animals overexpressing CED-10, ttx-1 mutants have fewer puncta, not more (Figure 2A). Thus, short NRE shape can derive from independent mechanisms.
claims.evidence: This conclusion is based on comparing the phenotypes of CED-10 overexpression and ttx-1 mutants.

claims.claim: Engulfment tracks neuron activity.
claims.source: Furthermore, that engulfment tracks neuron activity and modulating this process impacts animal behavior also suggests a physiological role for this process.
claims.evidence: This is supported by the data in Figure 6 showing that activity mutants have altered engulfment.

claims.claim: Modulating engulfment impacts animal behavior.
claims.source: Furthermore, that engulfment tracks neuron activity and modulating this process impacts animal behavior also suggests a physiological role for this process.
claims.evidence: This is supported by the data in Figure 7 showing that engulfment defects alter thermotaxis behavior.

claims.claim: Glial engulfment is an active regulator of neural functions.
claims.source: In summary, our findings reveal glial engulfment as an active regulator of neural functions.
claims.evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on all the data presented in the manuscript.

claims.claim: Engulfment may be a general mechanism by which glia dynamically modulate sensory perception and neural functions, across modalities, systems, and species.
claims.source: This raises the possibility that engulfment may be a general mechanism by which glia dynamically modulate sensory perception and neural functions, across modalities, systems, and species.
claims.evidence: This is a speculation based on the findings in C. elegans and the conservation of the molecular machinery.

results.result: AMsh glia engulf AFD neuron-receptive ending (NRE) microvilli, but not cilia, in adult C. elegans. Multiple microvilli-specific markers (SRTX-1, GCY-8, GCY-18, GCY-23) appear as puncta in glia, while the ciliary marker DYF-11 does not. Mutants lacking microvilli (ttx-1) have no glial puncta, whereas cilia-defective mutants (dyf-11, osm-6) retain or accumulate more puncta than wild type.
results.evaluation: Claims C22-C27 provide converging evidence from multiple independent approaches: (1) four different microvilli markers consistently show glial puncta while ciliary markers do not; (2) genetic ablation of microvilli eliminates puncta while ciliary defects increase them; (3) laser and genetic ablation of AFD neurons eliminate puncta. The multi-pronged experimental strategy strongly supports the conclusion that microvilli, not cilia, are the source of engulfed material.

results.result: AFD-derived glial puncta have an average size of 541 ± 145 nm, which is intermediate between exophers (~3.8 μm) and ciliary extracellular vesicles (~150 nm), and similar in size to individual AFD-NRE microvilli or cilia.
results.evaluation: Claims C10-C13 are supported by quantitative super-resolution microscopy (C10) and electron microscopy measurements (C13), with appropriate comparisons to previously characterized structures (C11-C12). The size measurements are consistent across techniques and support the interpretation that puncta represent individual or small groups of microvilli.

results.result: Glial engulfment of AFD-NRE occurs primarily in adults, not during development. Puncta are rarely found in embryos or early larvae, become detectable at L4, and increase in number during adulthood. Temperature affects puncta accumulation, with higher temperatures correlating with more puncta.
results.evaluation: Claims C14-C17 and C21 are supported by developmental time course data (Figure 2C-D) showing age-dependent accumulation and temperature-dependent differences (Figure 2E). Sample sizes are adequate (n=78 for day 1 adults, n=171 for population distribution). The data clearly demonstrate post-developmental engulfment with environmental modulation.

results.result: Individual puncta separate from the NRE at a frequency of 0.8 ± 0.3 events/min and travel at 1.05 ± 0.1 μm/s down the glial process toward the cell body, consistent with motor-protein-dependent retrograde trafficking.
results.evaluation: Claims C18-C19 are supported by time-lapse microscopy data (Videos 1-2, Figure 2—figure supplement 1B) with quantification from n=5 animals. The measured speeds are consistent with known motor protein velocities cited in the manuscript. However, the sample size is relatively small for dynamic measurements, and individual animal variability is not reported.

results.result: The phosphatidylserine (PS) flippase TAT-1/ATP8A regulates engulfment cell-autonomously in AFD neurons. Loss of tat-1 increases engulfment, and AFD-specific rescue fully restores wild-type levels. In contrast, mutations in apoptotic PS-exposure factors (ced-8, ced-3, scrm-1) have minimal or no effect on engulfment.
results.evaluation: Claims C28-C33 demonstrate that TAT-1 regulates engulfment through a mechanism distinct from apoptotic cell death. The cell-autonomous rescue experiment (C32) is critical evidence that TAT-1 functions in the neuron, not the glia. The epistasis and rescue data are convincing, though the 'presumptive null' designation for tat-1 could be better justified.

results.result: The phosphatidylserine receptor PSR-1 acts in glia downstream of TAT-1 to promote NRE engulfment. PSR-1 deletion dramatically reduces engulfment, glial-specific expression rescues the defect, and PSR-1 localizes to glial membranes around AFD-NRE. The PS-bridging molecule TTR-52 functions in the same pathway as PSR-1.
results.evaluation: Claims C36-C43 provide strong evidence for PSR-1 as the glial PS receptor through multiple approaches: loss-of-function, cell-specific rescue, localization, epistasis with tat-1, and genetic interaction with ttr-52. The epistasis experiments (C40, C42) are particularly convincing. The localization data (C39) directly supports the proposed function.

results.result: CED-1/Draper/MEGF10, a major receptor for apoptotic cell engulfment and glial debris clearance in other contexts, is dispensable for AFD-NRE engulfment by AMsh glia. Surprisingly, ced-1 mutants show enhanced puncta numbers compared to wild type.
results.evaluation: Claims C34-C35 and C48 demonstrate that CED-1 is not required for engulfment initiation, distinguishing this process from apoptotic phagocytosis. The unexpected increase in puncta in ced-1 mutants (C48) is well-documented but mechanistically unclear. The authors suggest CED-1 may act downstream in phagolysosome maturation, which is plausible but requires further validation.

results.result: The α-integrin PAT-2, but not INA-1, regulates glial engulfment of AFD-NRE. PAT-2 RNAi significantly blocks engulfment and strongly enhances the defects of psr-1 mutants, suggesting PAT-2 and PSR-1 act together.
results.evaluation: Claims C44-C47 identify PAT-2 as a second receptor working with PSR-1. The genetic interaction data (C46) showing enhancement in psr-1 mutants is strong evidence for cooperative function. However, the reliance on RNAi rather than genetic mutants for PAT-2 is a limitation, as RNAi knockdown may be incomplete or variable.

results.result: The ternary GEF complex CED-2/CrkII, CED-5/DOCK180, and CED-12/ELMO1 regulates engulfment of AFD-NREs. Mutations in ced-2, ced-5, or ced-12 reduce glial puncta, and glial-specific expression of CED-12 rescues the defect.
results.evaluation: Claims C49-C51 demonstrate that the canonical GEF complex acts in this pathway. The cell-specific rescue (C50) confirms glial function. The data are consistent with the known role of this complex in apoptotic phagocytosis, supporting conservation of the molecular machinery.

results.result: The Rac1 GTPase CED-10 functions in glia downstream of CED-2/5/12 and PSR-1 to control engulfment. CED-10 loss-of-function or dominant-negative expression blocks engulfment, while overexpression increases it. CED-10 is both necessary and sufficient to regulate engulfment rates, and its activation is specific (not through UNC-73/TRIO).
results.evaluation: Claims C52-C62 provide comprehensive evidence for CED-10 as the central regulator of engulfment rate. The epistasis experiments (C55), rescue (glial-specific expression), and overexpression studies (C56, C61) are all consistent. The finding that CED-10 levels are rate-limiting (C62) is particularly important for the conclusion that glia actively drive engulfment.

results.result: Expression of constitutively active CED-10G12V results in reduced engulfed puncta, but the AFD-NRE is significantly shorter in these mutants, suggesting hyperefficient engulfment that depletes the NRE.
results.evaluation: Claims C59-C60 address an apparent paradox: constitutively active CED-10 has fewer puncta but shorter NRE. The interpretation that this reflects hyperefficient engulfment is reasonable and supported by the NRE length data (C60, Figure 7—figure supplement 1). However, alternative explanations (e.g., effects on NRE development) are not fully excluded.

results.result: The actin polymerization factor WSP-1/nWASp acts downstream of CED-10 to execute engulfment. Loss of wsp-1 blocks engulfment, while glial-specific overexpression increases it, suggesting CED-10-dependent actin remodeling is the rate-limiting step.
results.evaluation: Claims C63-C65 identify WSP-1 as the effector of CED-10 in engulfment. The loss-of-function and overexpression data parallel those for CED-10, supporting the proposed pathway. The conclusion that actin remodeling is rate-limiting (C65) is reasonable but somewhat speculative, as other factors could also be limiting.

results.result: AFD neuron activity reciprocally regulates engulfment levels. Mutants with reduced activity (tax-2, tax-4; cng-3) accumulate more puncta, while mutants with increased cGMP/activity (pde-1; pde-5) have fewer puncta. Acute chemogenetic silencing of AFD increases puncta within 24 hours.
results.evaluation: Claims C69-C74 demonstrate activity-dependent regulation of engulfment through multiple approaches: genetic mutants affecting CNG channels (C69-C71), cGMP levels (C72), and acute chemogenetic silencing (C73). The reciprocal effects and acute response strongly support the conclusion that activity dynamically regulates engulfment.

results.result: Neuron activity controls NRE engulfment through the CED-10 pathway. The increased puncta in tax-2 mutants is suppressed by loss of ced-10, psr-1, or pat-2, and ced-10 loss suppresses the effect of acute AFD silencing.
results.evaluation: Claims C75-C78 use epistasis analysis to place activity regulation upstream of the engulfment machinery. The suppression experiments are well-designed and clearly demonstrate that activity signals through the identified molecular pathway. This is critical evidence that activity regulates engulfment rate rather than puncta degradation.

results.result: Glial engulfment regulates AFD-NRE microvilli length. Loss of ced-10 or dominant-negative CED-10 expression results in elongated microvilli, while CED-10 overexpression produces shorter microvilli. The defect worsens with age in overexpression strains.
results.evaluation: Claims C79-C84 establish a functional consequence of engulfment on NRE morphology. The bidirectional effects (longer with less engulfment, shorter with more) are consistent and support a direct role for engulfment in shaping the NRE. The age-dependent worsening (C82) suggests ongoing remodeling. However, the analysis is qualitative (defective vs. normal) rather than quantitative measurements of length.

results.result: AFD-NRE engulfment by AMsh glia is required for appropriate thermotaxis behavior. ced-10 mutants exhibit altered thermosensory behavior (preferring cooler temperatures), and animals overexpressing CED-10 in glia show athermotactic defects regardless of cultivation temperature.
results.evaluation: Claims C88-C91 demonstrate that engulfment defects cause behavioral phenotypes. The thermotaxis assays (Figure 7C-F) show clear differences between wild type and engulfment mutants. The glial-specific overexpression causing behavioral defects (C90) is particularly strong evidence. However, the behavioral assays measure population distributions, and individual animal tracking would strengthen the conclusions.

results.result: The behavioral defects are consistent with activity-dependent engulfment regulating NRE shape and function. CED-10 overexpression mimics tax-2 mutant behavior (both have increased puncta and reduced activity), while ced-10 mutants show cryophilic behavior similar to mutants with increased cGMP.
results.evaluation: Claims C92-C94 integrate the activity, engulfment, morphology, and behavior data into a coherent model. The parallels between engulfment mutants and activity mutants (C92-C93) support the proposed mechanism. However, this is correlative evidence, and the causal chain (activity → engulfment → morphology → behavior) has not been fully established with all intermediate steps measured in the same animals.

results.result: Glia actively drive neuronal remodeling rather than passively clearing debris. Evidence includes: (1) glial CED-10 levels modulate engulfment rates, NRE shape, and behavior; (2) short NRE can result from independent mechanisms (CED-10 overexpression vs. ttx-1 mutants have different puncta levels); (3) engulfment tracks neuron activity and modulating it impacts behavior.
results.evaluation: Claims C96-C122 synthesize the evidence for active glial control. The three lines of reasoning are logical: (1) rate control by glial factors, (2) dissociation of NRE length from puncta number, (3) activity-dependent regulation with behavioral consequences. However, the distinction between 'active' and 'passive' is somewhat semantic, and the evidence primarily shows that glia can modulate engulfment rate, not necessarily that they initiate it independently of neuronal signals.

results.result: Glia-dependent phagocytosis in AMsh glia is dynamically tuned throughout animal life to modulate NRE morphology and behavior, distinguishing it from all-or-none apoptotic phagocytosis. This controlled phagocytosis may similarly regulate glial engulfment in other settings.
results.evaluation: Claim C102 is well-supported by the developmental time course, activity-dependent regulation, and behavioral consequences. The distinction from apoptotic phagocytosis is valid. However, claim C103 is speculative, extrapolating from C. elegans to other systems based on molecular conservation. This is a reasonable hypothesis but not directly tested.

results.result: Glial pruning uses distinct receptors compared to apoptotic phagocytosis. In C. elegans, apoptotic phagocytosis relies predominantly on CED-1 with PSR-1 playing a minor role, but AMsh glial pruning requires PSR-1 and not CED-1. This difference may reflect the size of engulfed particles.
results.evaluation: Claims C104-C107 highlight an important mechanistic distinction. The differential requirement for receptors is well-documented. The hypothesis that particle size determines receptor usage (C107) is supported by a citation to tail-spike cell debris engulfment, but this remains correlative and requires further testing.

results.result: The molecular machinery identified in C. elegans has mammalian orthologs with neurological functions. Murine ATP8A1/2 knockout mice show neurological deficits and shortened photoreceptor NRE. TTR-52 orthologs and PS-bridging opsonins function in mammalian glial engulfment.
results.evaluation: Claims C109-C112 are based entirely on citations to previous work. The cited studies support the conservation of molecular components, but the authors do not present new data on mammalian systems. The parallels are suggestive but do not directly demonstrate that the same mechanisms operate in mammals.

results.result: Glial pruning is conserved in both CNS and PNS and is executed for normal neural functions by analogous molecular mechanisms. AMsh glia and AFD neuron likely cooperate through multiple mechanisms to regulate NRE shape and thermosensory behavior.
results.evaluation: Claim C115 is supported by the demonstration that PNS glia (AMsh) use similar molecular machinery to CNS glia for pruning. Claim C116 acknowledges that engulfment is likely one of multiple regulatory mechanisms, which is appropriately cautious given the complexity of glia-neuron interactions. The citations to previous work from the same group support this broader context.

results.result: Background and contextual claims about C. elegans nervous system anatomy, AFD-NRE structure, thermotaxis behavior, and conservation of glial functions across species.
results.evaluation: These claims (C8-C9, C66-C68, C85-C87, C95, C108, C113-C114, C117) are primarily based on citations to established literature and provide necessary context for the study. They are well-supported by the cited references and represent accepted knowledge in the field. Claim C117 about the importance of thermosensory behavior is a reasonable inference but somewhat speculative.
